## Context

Backlog item **b-a8270f**, continued from `SA-0285`. Every line number
below was read at `11b4d93351baa6b9e9a0f67c08a736877ffe3071`, the head
`SA-0285` landed.

**`History` is the one model in `saffron/` with a model-level
`strict=True`.** `saffron/intake.py:164` sets
`History.model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)`. Every
other model checked sets `ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` alone: `Mutant`
(`:86`), `Criterion` (`:117`) and `Spec` (`:180`) in the same file;
`_SpecReviewFinding` (`saffron/spec_review.py:96`), `_SpecReviewFindings`
(`:107`) and `_SpecWriterReply` (`:537`); `_Reported`
(`saffron/phases/review.py:77`), `_ProbeAnswer` (`:416`) and
`_WrongVersionReport` (`:573`); `GateDeclaration`
(`saffron/repos/policy.py:46`), `IntegrityPatterns` (`:59`) and `Policy`
(`:67`).

**Every other departure from lax validation in this file carries its own
measured-reason comment, on the field alone.** `estimated_lines`
(`saffron/intake.py:214`) is `Field(default=None, gt=0, strict=True)`,
commented "Strict, since a lax `int` read `true` as 1 (measured
2026-09-22)". `estimate_measured` (`:216`) is `Field(default=False,
strict=True)`, commented "True when a prototype's diff was measured, so
no hand overrun applies (b-b0a187)". `History`'s `batches` (`:174`) is
`bool = False`, no `Field(...)`, no comment, and the strictness it
actually needs comes from the model-level setting two lines up instead.
`CLAUDE.md:213`: "A measured fact beats a reasoned one, and the comment
says which." The field-less, uncommented model-level setting breaks that
rule even though `tests/test_intake.py:684`'s
`test_a_history_declaration_parses_and_a_malformed_one_is_refused` shows
the behaviour it buys — refusing `'yes'` and `1` for `batches` — is
exactly the intended one.

**`command` does not need strict mode.** `command: str` (`:163`) takes
whatever `yaml.safe_load` hands it under that key once `parse_spec`
(`:264`) reads the frontmatter; a YAML scalar not already a string (an
int, say) is refused by a bare `str` field with no `strict=True` of its
own, confirmed against this pydantic build. The model-level `strict=True`
reaches `command` today for no measured reason; nothing in
`tests/test_intake.py` exercises a non-string `command` either way.

## Problem

In `saffron/intake.py`'s `History` model:

1. Drop `strict=True` from `model_config`, leaving
   `ConfigDict(extra="forbid")`, matching every other model in `saffron/`.
2. Move the strictness onto `batches` alone, as `Field(default=False,
   strict=True)`, with a measured-reason comment in the shape
   `estimated_lines` and `estimate_measured` already use: which lax values
   were wrongly accepted, and that this was measured rather than
   reasoned.
3. Leave `command: str` untouched. It is not swept into any strict scope.

No behaviour changes: `batches` still refuses `'yes'` and `1` and still
defaults to `False`; `command` is still refused when blank or missing;
an unknown key under `history` is still refused by `extra="forbid"`. The
existing witness,
`tests/test_intake.py::test_a_history_declaration_parses_and_a_malformed_one_is_refused`,
must keep passing unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Any change to what `History` accepts or refuses. This spec moves where
  a setting lives and adds the comment it was missing; it adds no new
  rule and removes none.
- `SA-0272` and anything that reads `History.command` or `.batches` at
  runtime. Nothing here touches a caller.
- The nine `strict=True` model-level settings checked above that are
  *not* present (i.e. every other model already matches the pattern this
  spec restores on `History`). None of them need a change.

## Notes for the agent

This edits existing code; it is not new code, so the acceptance criterion
declares `wrong_versions`, including the current build itself as the
first entry, and the `witness` gate should report a real pass here, not
`skip`.

`pydantic`'s `FieldInfo.metadata` carries a `pydantic.types.Strict(strict=True)`
marker for a field declared with `Field(..., strict=True)`, and carries
none for a bare field; the witness introspects `History.model_fields`
directly for this, alongside the unchanged behavioural checks (`'yes'`
and `1` refused, default `False` preserved), rather than relying on
behaviour alone to tell the three wrong versions apart from the right one.

`estimated_lines` here is a prototype's measured diff: 416 changed
tokens over the one source file and one test file in `touches`, moving
the strict setting and adding the one new witness.
